goal: Extract sub-concepts by projecting out meta-concept directions from transported residual, then reading what remains. No prompt needed → no prompt contamination.
approach: 1. Forward pass with concern prompt → get transported residual h at L26
2. Get concept direction v_word = unembed[token_id] for each meta-concept
4. Read top-k tokens of h_sub → 'what the residual thinks about EXCEPT the meta-concept'

results.before_projection: Fiber (3.2%), fiber (2.2%), diet (0.03%) — correct broad concepts
results.after_projecting_fiber_alpha_1.0: listed (0.0000), cholesterol (0.0000) — cholesterol is a real sub-concept but signal too weak
results.after_subspace_projection_orthogonalized: fiber 99.98% — projection INCREASED fiber probability (QR orthogonalization misaligned)

root_cause: Unembedding concept directions are highly non-orthogonal in 3584-dim space. Projecting out one concept direction destroys most of the signal because concept directions are entangled. Even alpha=0.5 collapses probabilities to ~0.
what_would_be_needed: Template Lens (paper Appendix A.9.1): pre-compute whitened concept vectors via Stein's lemma approximation. Whitening (Σ+λI)^{-1} orthogonalizes the directions, making projection safe. But this requires ~100 forward passes per word to build template vectors — significant precomputation cost.

two_pass_concern.method: Couple meta-concept into prompt for Pass 2

conclusion: Residual space projection is NOT viable with simple linear projection due to non-orthogonal concept directions. Two-pass concern (Phase 24, 26% hierarchy) remains the best approach. Next step: parallel prompt variant comparison to improve the 26% rate.
